# Summary

In this report, we began by looking for statistically significant differences between groups (*i.e.* dentists and residents). We examined comfort levels, clinical practices, knowledge, and quiz results. We then looked at the residency program for each respondent (current and past residents) to see if that informed differences in responses, and then within practicing dentists, analyzed whether tenure in their practice contributed to differences in their responses. Finally, additional analysis questions were conducted to find out how familiarity with guidelines contributed to findings of substance use in practice, and other comparisons along those lines.  
All hypothesis tests were conducted using a Fisher exact test at the $\alpha$ = 0.05 significance level.  Each family of tests was adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing using the Benjamini- Hochberg (BH) adjustment to control the false discover rate (FDR) at 0.05. After adjustment, we found that 1 out of the 16 tests in the comfort and clinical practice analysis was significant.  No other statistically significant results were found in any of the knowledge, quiz, or environment groups.  Additionally, no significant results were found in the dentist practice analysis, though several results were significant prior to adjustment.  Finally, 17 of the 18 tests performed in the additional analysis section were found to be significant even after adjusting with BH.  

All hypothesis test results are reported in the significant findings section, and their significance before and after the B-H adjustment is presented.

# Methods

We tested for associations between questions and differences in proportions across groups (residents vs directors) using Fisher exact tests. Low p-value's indicate significant results.  We adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing via the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure to control false discovery rate (FDR) at 0.05.  

For questions with multiple parts, we split them into individual questions (e.g. 8a, 8b, 8c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc.

Finally we present data visualizations to summarize the results. Interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section with all plots appearing in are in the Appendix.

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

library(gt)
set.seed(1)
```

```{r, echo = F}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}
```

# Significant Findings

Below are several tables outlining each of the categories of analysis requested.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
  #table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
  }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}
```

## Resident/Dentist Comfort & Clinical Practice Analysis

Below is a table comparing residents and dentists comfort levels and clinical practices.  We find one comparison to be statistically significant.

Significant results found here: 

<!-- Q8h, Q9, Q8a, and Q8k, all compared to the role (resident/dentist): This means that for each of the following questions, dentists and residents' responses differed significantly in regards to comfort level/clinical practices -->

<!-- Q8h: Determining when an oral soft-tissue finding warrants referral or biopsy -->

<!-- Q8a: Recognizing oral soft-tissue changes associated with cigarette smoking in adolescents -->

<!-- Q8k: Knowledge and understanding of current AAPD guidelines related to substance-use, anticipatory guidance, and management -->

 - Q9: How often do you screen patients for tobacco, vaping/ENDS, or other substance use?

```{r resident-dentist-comfort, echo = FALSE}
qref = c("Q8a",  "Q8b",  "Q8c",  "Q8d",  "Q8e",  "Q8f", "Q8g",  "Q8h" , "Q8i" , "Q8j" , "Q8k" , "Q9" ,  "Q10a" ,"Q10b", "Q11a" ,"Q11b")
n <- length(qref)
comfort_dic <- data.frame(
  q_ref = qref, 
  role = c(rep("role", n))
)

comfort_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(), 
  Test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(comfort_dic))) {
  
  comfort_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = comfort_dic$q_ref[i],
    question2 = comfort_dic$role[i],
    data = m_coalesced
  )
}

comfort_results <- comfort_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = comfort_dic$q_ref, 
    Question2 = comfort_dic$role
  ) %>% 
  arrange(Adj_P)

comfort_results
```

## Dentist/Practice Analysis

```{r, echo = FALSE}

  q_ref = c("Q8a",  "Q8b",  "Q8c",  "Q8d",  "Q8e",  "Q8f", "Q8g",  "Q8h" , "Q8i" , "Q8j" , "Q8k" , "Q9" ,  "Q10a" ,"Q10b", "Q11a", "Q11b","Q12", "score"),

prac_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),

  Significant = logical(),
```

## Additional Analysis

Nearly all comparisons tested in this group were found to be significant even after adjusting for multiple hypothesis testing.  


```{r aditional-analysis, echo = FALSE}
addt_dic <- data.frame(
  q_ref = c("Q8a",  "Q8b",  "Q8c",  "Q8d",  "Q8e",  "Q8f", "Q8g",  "Q8h" , "Q8i" , "Q8j" , "Q8k" , "Q9" ,  "Q10a" ,"Q10b", "Q11a", "Q11b", "Q10a", "Q10b"), 
  q_group = c(rep("Q12", 14), "Q9", "Q9", "Q13", "Q13")
)

addt_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(), 
  Test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(addt_dic))) {
  
  addt_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = addt_dic$q_ref[i],
    question2 = addt_dic$q_group[i],
    data = m_coalesced
  )
}

addt_results <- addt_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = addt_dic$q_ref, 
    Question2 = addt_dic$q_group
  ) %>% 
  arrange(Adj_P)

addt_results

```
Test's that were found to be significant were: 

 - Q8: All topics of comfort level (except Q8h) vs Q12: Familiarity with AAPD policies
 - Q9: Screening frequency for substances vs Q12: Familiarity with AAPD policies
 - Q10a, Q10b: What age to begin screening + providing guidance for substance use vs Q12: Familiarity with AAPD policies
 - Q10a, Q10b: What age to begin screening + providing guidance for substance use vs Q13: What age should anticipatory guidance and counseling regarding tobacco vaping/ENDS, and substance misuse begin?
 - Q11a, Q11b: Substances identified through history + oral findings vs Q9: Frequency of screening patients for substance use

Below are plots comparing each additional analysis question (Q11a and Q11b were excluded from visualizations because there were too many categories).

```{r, echo = F}
plots_addt <- pmap(addt_dic %>% filter(q_ref %notin% c("Q11a","Q11b")), 
                      function(q_ref, q_group){
                        stack_bar(
                          q_reference = q_ref, 
                          q_group = q_group,
                          data = m_coalesced
                        )
                      })
walk(plots_addt, print)
```

```{r, echo = F}
plots_comfort <- pmap(comfort_dic %>% filter(q_ref %notin% c("Q11a","Q11b")), 
                   function(q_ref, role){
                     stack_bar(
                       q_reference = q_ref, 
                       q_group = role,
                       data = m_coalesced
                     )
                   })
walk(plots_comfort, print)
```

## Knowledge Plots

Below are all plots comparing the knowledge of residents versus dentists.

```{r, echo = F}
plots_knowledge <- pmap(knowledge_dic %>% filter(q_ref %notin% c("Q11a","Q11b")), 
                      function(q_ref, role){
                        stack_bar(
                          q_reference = q_ref, 
                          q_group = role,
                          data = m_coalesced
                        )
                      })
walk(plots_knowledge, print)
```
